title: Reviewing two names after a supplied learning exchange
summary: A short name review following an explicitly authored learning prefix in the same session. Both methods receive the same introductions; the acknowledgments establish exposure, not successful learning. No earlier-week lesson or photographs are assumed.

therapist.context: Continue the supplied learning exchange by discussing the two names and the links used to remember them. This is a spoken-name task without photographs.
objectives: Give the patient an opportunity to recall the names and talk about what helps them remember. Use their actual response to decide whether to explore a link, offer support or move on.
materials: First name: Tan Mei Li. The supplied learning link is Mei Li with beautiful.
Second name: Lim Chong Wei. The supplied link is badminton player Lee Chong Wei; the exercise surname is Lim.
The names were introduced in the supplied prefix. Acknowledgments do not establish successful learning. There is no previous-week lesson or visual material.
therapist.opening_question: We went through two names and some ways to remember them. Can you recall the first person's name?
conversation_plan: Follow the patient's recall attempt. Acknowledge what they retrieved, and respond to any uncertainty or explanation rather than treating every reply as just correct or incorrect.

Explore how a name or link came to mind when that follows the answer. If recall is difficult, offer a supplied association, explain it or provide the missing name; allow time for the patient's response.

Bring the other name into the conversation when it fits. Move between recall, explanation and feedback according to the patient's replies; these are possible directions, not a fixed sequence of tests.
response_guidance: Keep an unaided question free of the target answer. Repetition can help after a cue or correction, but do not add repeated testing simply because the patient has answered correctly.

Use the supplied links when referring to the lesson. Discuss a new patient suggestion as their suggestion, not a link already taught. Explain a mismatch supportively and offer useful information instead of repeatedly demanding the same answer.
completion_criteria: The names and relevant remembering strategies have been discussed as far as useful, or the patient wants to pause or stop. Correct recall and a particular explanation are not required.
